VG25 is VG24 with one added parameter. A child's **signed share of comprehension at their previous administration wave** — how much of what they understood, they signed — relative to their own persistent signing standing, shifts the logit of the production ratio $q$ they show now. One coefficient, $\beta_{sign\,lag}$, carries it, and VG24 is nested exactly at $\beta_{sign\,lag}=0$.

The question it exists to answer was asked on 2026-09-04 and has never had a fitted model behind it: **does signing earlier predict speaking more later?**

## Three questions that sound like one {#sec-three-quantities}

"Does signing help speech?" is three different statistical questions, and the single most likely way to misread this page is to take $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ as the answer to all three. The project now carries an estimate of each, and naming which is which is part of the deliverable.

| Question | Quantity | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Do the children who sign more of what they understand also **say** more of it, as a persistent standing? | $\rho_{sign\,q}$, a between-child correlation | VG24 |
| At a given moment, within one child's understood vocabulary, do saying and signing a word go together? | $\psi$, a within-child, within-comprehension association | VG15 / VG24 / this model |
| Does a child who signed **more than usual for them** at an earlier wave go on to say a larger share of what they understand **later**? | $\beta_{sign\,lag}$, a prospective within-child effect | **this model** |

They can legitimately differ in sign. Children who sign more may say less at a given moment ($\psi$) while the children who sign more overall are also the children who say more overall ($\rho_{sign\,q}$), and neither settles what happens to one child over time ($\beta_{sign\,lag}$).

There is a fourth, descriptive, result that is close to this model's estimand but not identical to it. [`notes/202608160930`](../../notes/202608160930-early-signing-and-later-speech.md) found, among 147 children and holding earlier speech **and** comprehension standing fixed, that the signed share of comprehension predicts later spoken vocabulary at $+0.19$ SD per SD, 89% ETI $[0.03, 0.36]$, stable under study fixed effects and single-study deletion. That is a two-wave residual regression, not a model, and it **conditions on the child's speech at the earlier wave**, which a $q$ child intercept — the child's average across all waves — does not do. So the note and this model are companions, not replacements, and their numbers should not be expected to coincide.

## Why the lag extends VG24 and not VG15 {#sec-why-vg24}

Because otherwise the coefficient would be measuring the wrong thing, and doing it badly.

[`notes/202608151140`](../../notes/202608151140-cross-lag-not-for-models-of-record.md) §3 established, on VG16, that within-child deviations in this pool have **no memory beyond the occasion**. A lag predictor measured relative to the *population* therefore mostly carries the covariance between children's *persistent* standings — which is exactly $\rho_{sign\,q}$, reached through a proxy with attenuation to argue about. With VG24's correlated child block in the model, that persistent association has somewhere proper to live, and the lag is left measuring what it is named for.

Two consequences follow, and both are registered rather than argued:

- The baseline is **within-child** (@sec-baseline), not VG16's population-relative one.
- VG25 derives from VG24's definition, so VG24 is its exact nested null and VG24's own fingerprint is untouched.

## The four design decisions {#sec-design}

[#297](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/297) named four choices that had to be made before this model could be registered, and measurement added a fifth. Each is stated with what decided it, because each moves either the estimand or the evidence.

### Which likelihoods the lag enters {#sec-scope}

**Registered: the spoken marginal *and* the cross-tab compositions.**

VG15 keeps its **child shifts** out of the four-cell and produced-cell Dirichlet-Multinomials, deliberately: a free per-child offset is co-identified with the association $\psi$ on those thin rows, and letting it in moved $\psi$ from $1.78$ to about $2.8$. Treating the lag the same way would confine it to the spoken marginal.

That is not the same decision, and the difference is why it was taken differently. $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ is **one scalar multiplying a covariate fixed by the data**: it adds a single dimension to the parameter space, not one per child, and it has no per-child freedom with which to chase a composition. Set against that, confining it costs most of the evidence — measured on the 2026-09-11 frame, **191 supporting observations from 129 children, against 111 from 80**, with `uk_07` contributing nothing at all under the narrow arm because its rows carry no spoken marginal.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The caveat that comes with it

Under the within-child baseline the predictor itself contains the child's signing intercept **at the prior wave**. So an estimated per-child quantity does reach the composition — through one scalar coefficient, on lagged rows only, rather than as a free offset per row. The `sign-lag-population` sensitivity is the arm in which no estimated per-child quantity reaches the cells at all, because that baseline subtracts the shift back out. Reading it beside `sign-lag-marginal-only` is what says whether $\psi$ moved, and why.
:::

### The baseline {#sec-baseline}

**Registered: within-child.** The predictor is the prior wave's signed-share logit minus the model's expectation for *that child* at that wave, so a child is compared with their own persistent signing standing rather than with the population's.

VG16 registered the **population-relative** baseline for its own lag, and the difference between the two models is not an inconsistency. VG16 carries no $\rho_{uq}$, so its population baseline still had a between-child association to measure. VG25 inherits $\rho_{sign\,q}$, so that baseline would be a second, noisier reading of a quantity already in the model. It is registered as the `sign-lag-population` sensitivity, where it doubles as the check described above.

### `nz_01`'s denominator {#sec-nz01}

**Registered: `nz_01` supplies no lag source.** Its cross-tab partitions *produced* words, so the only share it measures is the signed share of **production** — a different variable, not a differently-denominated version of this one. Putting the two under one coefficient would make $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ mean two things at once. Its rows still enter every likelihood they always did.

On the current frame the decision costs nothing measurable: no `nz_01` child has an earlier wave carrying a comprehension-denominated share, so those children would consume no lag either way. The rule is registered on the argument rather than on the count, so that new `nz_01` follow-up data cannot quietly change what the coefficient means.

### The gap {#sec-gap}

The model assumes **one coefficient across every gap it sees**. A prospective association measured over a year is not obviously the same quantity as one measured over three months, and nothing in the graph says so — the assumption [#242](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/242) asked to be checked rather than asserted. The `sign-lag-gap-12` arm is registered with the model rather than after a reviewer asks for it. @sec-support reports the gap distribution this fit actually rests on.

### Boundary shares: the fifth decision, which measurement forced {#sec-boundary}

**Registered: the continuity correction, not VG16's clip.**

The predictor is $\mathrm{logit}(\text{signed}/\text{understood})$, and a signed share of exactly $0$ is common here in a way an understood count of exactly $0$ is not. On the 2026-09-11 frame **26 of the 191 supporting rows** have a source wave at which the child signed none of what they understood, and 2 more at which they signed all of it — **14.7% of the support on a logit boundary**, against 7 of VG16's 477 rows (1.5%).

The clip puts all 26 at $\mathrm{logit}(10^{-4}) = -9.21$ whatever the wave measured, so a child who understood 2 words and signed none enters identically to a child who understood 406 and signed none. Those 28 rows then carry **76.1% of the predictor's total sum of squares** — which is to say the coefficient would be estimated mostly off a floor constant. The continuity correction $(k+0.5)/(n+1)$ derives each from its own wave's denominator instead: $-1.61$ for the 2-word wave, $-6.70$ for the 406-word one. It halves the predictor's SD ($3.34 \rightarrow 1.79$) and the boundary's leverage ($76.1\% \rightarrow 45.8\%$).

`sign-lag-clip` is the arm that measures the difference on a fit rather than on this arithmetic.

## What identifies the coefficient {#sec-support}

::: {.callout-important}
## Most of the frame does not inform this parameter

A row informs $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ only if the child has an **earlier** administration wave carrying a signed share of comprehension, and the row itself enters a likelihood the lag term reaches. For every other row the predictor is identically zero. That is a minority of the frame, and the interval this model reports is the interval that minority supports.
:::

```{python}

    _audit = _pd.read_csv("sign_cross_lag_audit.csv")
    _branch = _audit["branch"].fillna("")
    _supporting = _audit[_branch != ""]

    print("| | Observations | Children |")
    print("| --- | ---: | ---: |")
    print(f"| With a prior-wave signed-share source | {len(_audit):,} | "
          f"{_audit['subject_code'].nunique():,} |")
    print(f"| Of those, reached by the lag term | {len(_supporting):,} | "
          f"{_supporting['subject_code'].nunique():,} |")
    print()
    print(": Rows with a source but no supporting likelihood carry a lag that "
          "informs nothing.")
    print()

    if len(_supporting):
        _gaps = _supporting["gap_months"]
        print(f"The supporting rows reach back a median of **{_gaps.median():.0f} "
              f"months** (IQR {_gaps.quantile(.25):.0f}–{_gaps.quantile(.75):.0f}, "
              f"range {_gaps.min():.0f}–{_gaps.max():.0f}), and the source signed "
              f"share runs {_supporting['source_signed_share'].min():.2f} to "
              f"{_supporting['source_signed_share'].max():.2f} "
              f"(median {_supporting['source_signed_share'].median():.2f}).")
        print()
        _boundary = int(_supporting["source_share_zero"].sum()) + int(
            _supporting["source_share_one"].sum()
        )
        print(f"**{_boundary} of {len(_supporting)}** sit at a share of exactly 0 "
              f"or exactly 1, where @sec-boundary's treatment decides the value.")
        print()
        print("| Study | Supporting observations | Children |")
        print("| --- | ---: | ---: |")
        for _study, _rows in _supporting.groupby("study"):
            print(f"| `{_study}` | {len(_rows):,} | {_rows['subject_code'].nunique():,} |")
        print()
        print("| Likelihood branch | Supporting observations |")
        print("| --- | ---: |")
        for _name, _count in _supporting["branch"].value_counts().items():
            print(f"| {_name} | {_count:,} |")
        print()
        print(": `conditional` and `marginal` are the spoken marginal's two "
              "branches; `cells` and `produced-cells` are the cross-tab "
              "compositions, which the lag reaches only under "
              "`sign_lag_in_cells`.")
except Exception as _exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a report must not fail on a missing artefact
    print(f"_Support tables unavailable: {type(_exc).__name__}._")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## The reporter confound, and what it does to a lag

Every count on this page comes from **one questionnaire completed by one parent**. For VG24's correlations that inflates the association, because a parent who over-reports over-reports every modality at once. A lag is partly protected: the predictor and the outcome come from **different administrations**, often months apart, so a single occasion's reporting tendency cannot produce both. What is *not* removed is a parent who persistently over-reports across visits — which the within-child baseline also partly absorbs, since it compares a child with their own average.

This is a reason to prefer the lag as evidence of direction, not a claim that it is unconfounded.
:::

## Priors {#sec-priors}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from vocab_growth.report_cells import render_priors_table

render_priors_table()
```

Every prior is VG24's, unchanged, including the LKJ concentration $\eta = 2$ on the child-effect correlation and the three $\mathrm{HalfNormal}(1.5)$ child scales. The one addition is $\beta_{sign\,lag} \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0, 0.5)$ — VG16's prior for its own lag, deliberately, so that the two coefficients are prior-comparable and a difference between them is a difference in the data.

::: {.callout-note}
## A symmetric prior is not a calibrated one

$\mathrm{Normal}(0, 0.5)$ imposes no direction, which is what the question requires: the model must be able to return a negative coefficient. Symmetry is not the same as being uninformative about magnitude, and an interval that excludes zero should be shown to do so under other scales before it is reported as a result. `beta-sign-tight` ($\sigma = 0.25$) and `beta-sign-wide` ($\sigma = 1.0$) are registered for that, and @sec-contraction reports how much this prior was actually narrowed by the data.
:::

## Findings {#sec-findings}

### The sign → speech cross-lag

```{python}
#| label: beta-sign-lag
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# Read from this fit's own diagnostics so the text cannot drift from the model
# it describes. The contraction check below is deliberate: a headline parameter
# that came back as its own prior is the failure mode VG24's LKJ defect taught,
# and it is not visible in a posterior interval alone.
import pandas as _pd

try:
    _diagnostics = _pd.read_csv("diagnostics.csv", index_col=0)
    if "beta_sign_lag" not in _diagnostics.index:
        raise KeyError("beta_sign_lag")
    _row = _diagnostics.loc["beta_sign_lag"]

    print("| Parameter | Posterior mean | SD | 89% ETI | ESS (bulk) | R-hat |")
    print("| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |")
    print(
        f"| $\\beta_{{sign\\,lag}}$ (`beta_sign_lag`) | {_row['mean']:.3f} | "
        f"{_row['sd']:.3f} | {_row['eti89_lb']:.3f} to {_row['eti89_ub']:.3f} | "
        f"{_row['ess_bulk']:,.0f} | {_row['r_hat']:.3f} |"
    )
    print()
    print(": Under VG24 this is exactly zero by construction.")
    print()

    # Did the data move it? A prior SD of 0.5 is the registered value; the
    # manifest is the authority, so read it where available.
    _prior_sd = 0.5
    try:
        import json as _json

        with open("fit_manifest.json", encoding="utf-8") as _fh:
            _prior_sd = float(
                _json.load(_fh)["model"]["definition"]["beta_sign_lag_sigma"]
            )
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - fall back to the registered value
        pass
    _contraction = 1 - _row["sd"] / _prior_sd
    print(
        f"The posterior SD is {_row['sd']:.3f} against a prior SD of "
        f"{_prior_sd:g}, a contraction of {_contraction:.2f}. "
        + (
            "The data moved this parameter."
            if _contraction > 0.2
            else "**The data barely moved this parameter**, so the interval "
            "below is close to the prior and should not be read as a result."
        )
    )
    print()

    if _row["eti89_lb"] > 0:
        _verdict = (
            "lies entirely **above** zero: a child who signed a larger share of "
            "what they understood than is usual for them goes on to say a larger "
            "share of what they understand later"
        )
    elif _row["eti89_ub"] < 0:
        _verdict = (
            "lies entirely **below** zero: signing more than usual at an earlier "
            "wave is followed by saying *less* later. That is the substitution "
            "reading, and it would have to be reconciled with the prospective "
            "descriptive result before being reported"
        )
    else:
        _verdict = (
            "**spans** zero, so this fit does not distinguish the prospective "
            "effect from the independence VG24 assumes. Given the support in "
            "@sec-support that is the outcome to expect rather than a surprise"
        )
    print(
        f"**This is the number the model exists to produce.** Its 89% "
        f"equal-tailed interval {_verdict}. Read it with @sec-support and "
        f"@sec-three-quantities: it is a prospective within-child effect on a "
        f"minority of the frame, not a population claim and not a restatement "
        f"of $\\rho_{{sign\\,q}}$."
    )
except Exception as _exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a report must not fail on a missing artefact
    print(f"_Cross-lag table unavailable: {type(_exc).__name__}._")
```

### In interpretable units

A coefficient on a logit scale answers no one's question. What it is worth is how far along the production-ratio trajectory a child is moved by signing one standard deviation more than usual for them — and that is the figure the deliverable should carry, alongside the gap and leave-one-study-out sensitivities.

```{python}
#| label: beta-sign-lag-units
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# Translate the coefficient into the predictor's own units: one SD of the
# realised lag predictor across the supporting rows. The predictor's baseline is
# estimated, so this uses the raw source logit, which is the part a reader can
# see in the audit file; the resulting shift is therefore a scale, not a
# posterior quantity, and is reported as such.
#
# The boundary treatment is read from THIS fit's manifest rather than assumed.
# A sensitivity variant renders the model of record's template, so
# `sign-lag-clip` would otherwise be described in the registered arm's units --
# and on this predictor that is not a rounding difference: the two treatments
# give SDs of 3.34 and 1.79 (@sec-boundary).
try:
    import json as _json

    import numpy as _np
    import pandas as _pd

    _audit = _pd.read_csv("sign_cross_lag_audit.csv")
    _supporting = _audit[_audit["branch"].fillna("") != ""]
    _diagnostics = _pd.read_csv("diagnostics.csv", index_col=0)
    _beta = _diagnostics.loc["beta_sign_lag"]

    with open("fit_manifest.json", encoding="utf-8") as _fh:
        _treatment = _json.load(_fh)["model"]["definition"]["sign_lag_zero_handling"]

    _share = _supporting["source_signed_share"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    _understood = _supporting["source_understood"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    if _treatment == "continuity":
        _corrected = (_share * _understood + 0.5) / (_understood + 1.0)
    else:
        _corrected = _np.clip(_share, 1e-4, 1 - 1e-4)
    _source_logit = _np.log(_corrected) - _np.log1p(-_corrected)
    _sd = float(_np.std(_source_logit))

    print(
        f"Across the {len(_supporting):,} supporting rows the source signed-share "
        f"logit has an SD of **{_sd:.2f}** under this fit's `{_treatment}` boundary "
        f"treatment. One SD of it shifts the production-ratio logit by "
        f"{_beta['mean'] * _sd:+.3f} "
        f"(89% ETI {_beta['eti89_lb'] * _sd:+.3f} to {_beta['eti89_ub'] * _sd:+.3f})."
    )
    print()
    print(
        "The shift in **words spoken** depends on where on the trajectory the "
        "child sits, because the logit is nonlinear: the same shift is worth "
        "more words in the middle of the range than at either end. The "
        "trajectory comparison against VG24 below is what turns it into words."
    )
except Exception as _exc:  # noqa: BLE001
    print(f"_Unit conversion unavailable: {type(_exc).__name__}._")
```

Four comparisons are worth making once there are numbers, and none is automatic:

- **Against VG24**, which is nested at $\beta_{sign\,lag}=0$. The population trajectories and $\psi$ should sit close — the criterion VG16 met against VG10, where the largest movement anywhere was 2.6 words understood and 2.0 words spoken. A material move in $\psi$ is something to explain, not to expect, and @sec-scope says which arm to read next if one appears.
- **Against $\rho_{sign\,q}$ from the same fit.** VG25 carries both, which is what makes the between-child and prospective quantities separable in one model rather than argued about across two. A large $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ with $\rho_{sign\,q}$ unchanged from VG24 is the clean result; both moving together is the case where the two are competing for the same evidence.
- **Against the descriptive $+0.19$** of [`notes/202608160930`](../../notes/202608160930-early-signing-and-later-speech.md), with the estimand difference stated (@sec-three-quantities): that regression conditions on earlier *speech*, which this model does not.
- **Against the sensitivities**, in this order of importance: `sign-lag-clip` (@sec-boundary), `sign-lag-marginal-only` and `sign-lag-population` (@sec-scope), `sign-lag-uk07-marginal`, `sign-lag-gap-12` (@sec-gap), then the two prior scales.

::: {.callout-note}
With the lag in the model, the reported population curve is the curve for **a child whose previous-wave signing was exactly at expectation**, rather than simply the population level. On the current frame the predictor is zero for the large majority of rows, so the two coincide for most of the pool — but the interpretive shift is real and is one of the reasons [`notes/202608151140`](../../notes/202608151140-cross-lag-not-for-models-of-record.md) argued against putting a lag in a model of record.
:::

## Association psi {#sec-psi}

![Posterior distribution of the sign–speech association. Mass to the right of 1 is evidence of positive association.](psi_posterior.png){#fig-psi .lightbox fig-align="left"}

$\psi$ is the second of @sec-three-quantities' three: a within-child, within-comprehension association between saying a word and signing it, at one moment. Unlike VG24, this model's lag term **does** reach the likelihoods that identify $\psi$ (@sec-scope), so a move against VG24 is possible here in a way it is not there, and is exactly what the `sign-lag-marginal-only` arm is registered to measure.

::: {.callout-warning}
## LOO leaks across the lag

Leaving one observation out of the likelihood does not remove it from the **later** observations whose lag predictor it feeds, so the out-of-sample figures on this page are optimistic for a lag model in a way they are not for VG24. This is the leakage [#242](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/242) raised against VG16 and it applies here unchanged; `scripts/wave_forward_score.py` is the forward-scoring answer to it, and it is the comparison to trust over the LOO table above.
:::

## Limits {#sec-limits}

- **This is a prospective association, not a causal effect of signing.** Nothing here randomises who signs. A child who signed more than usual at one wave may differ in intervention, environment or phenotype in ways the model does not observe, and the within-child baseline removes only the part of that which is constant for the child.
- **The coefficient rests on a minority of the frame** (@sec-support), and which children have an earlier wave carrying a signed share is an artefact of which studies followed children longitudinally and at what intervals. A coefficient reported as a property of children with Down syndrome is estimated from a subset defined by study design.
- **There is no leave-one-study-out arm yet.** [#297](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/297) check 5 asks for one, and it cannot be registered on this definition today: `exclude_studies` is a `BivariateModelDefinition` field, and adding it to `JointModelDefinition` would restale every VG15 and VG24 fit — a change to make deliberately, with the refit it costs, not as a side effect of registering a variant. `sign-lag-uk07-marginal` is the nearest thing available and is a different question: it keeps `uk_07`'s children and moves their rows from the cross-tab branch to the marginal one.
- **One coefficient across every gap** (@sec-gap). A prospective association over a year and one over three months are assumed to be the same quantity, and `sign-lag-gap-12` is the check rather than the fix.
- **The boundary treatment is a modelling choice, not a measurement** (@sec-boundary). Roughly one supporting row in seven has a source share of exactly 0 or 1, where the value the predictor takes is set by the correction rather than by the data.
- **Out-of-sample figures leak across the lag** (@sec-loo).
- **Parameter recovery is registered but not complete.** [#297](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/297)'s gate 4 asks for recovery in three designed cells — $(\beta = 0, \rho \neq 0)$, $(\beta \neq 0, \rho = 0)$ and both nonzero — whose purpose is to show the lag can be told apart from the correlation. VG25 is a registered recovery target and the simulator selects the wave-sequential order for it automatically, but two of those cells need a way to *set* a parameter in the truth draw, which the harness does not yet have. VG16's own recovery returned `beta_lag` 29% low on its one assessable replicate at `test` ([`notes/202609111500`](../../notes/202609111500-vg16-recovery-and-the-blocker-that-was-not-there.md)), so this check needs a tier above `test` when it runs.
- **No role has been assigned.** VG25 is `UNCLASSIFIED` in the catalogue, which fails closed: it keeps full publication strictness and stays in the default refit scope. Whether it becomes a model of record, a development step, or neither is a study-owner decision taken with [#190](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/issues/190)'s other scope questions.
